title: Reconciling Privacy with Provenance for Language Model Watermarks
abstract: arXiv:2611.06100v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Watermarking has great potential for regulating the use of language models (LMs), but its deployment has been marred by controversy, as many users argue that fine-grained tracking of LM usage violates their privacy. This tension reduces the effectiveness of watermarks, as users engage in evasion strategies such as paraphrasing that can remove much of the watermark signal. We show that provenance and privacy can be reconciled if we shift the goal of watermark design from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage. We develop locally differentially private watermarks which provably limit the evidence that any individual text can contribute to detection, while still enabling accurate estimation of population frequencies. translated_title: 调和隐私与溯源：面向语言模型水印的平衡之道
translated_abstract: 水印技术在规范语言模型（LM）的使用方面具有巨大潜力，但其部署一直饱受争议，因为许多用户认为对语言模型使用的细粒度追踪侵犯了他们的隐私。这种矛盾削弱了水印的有效性，因为用户会采取改写等规避策略，而这些策略可以去除大部分水印信号。我们证明，如果将水印设计的目标从追踪个体转变为估计总体使用情况，就可以调和溯源与隐私之间的矛盾。我们开发了本地差分隐私水印，可以从可证明的层面限制任何单个文本对检测所能贡献的证据，同时仍能实现对总体频率的准确估计。我们提出了红绿序列水印，这是一种具有隐私保护且计算高效的水印方法，能够在高隐私保护水平下，跨多种模型、样本量和生成场景实现准确的频率估计。
tldr: 提出红绿序列（RGS）本地差分隐私水印，通过将水印目标从追踪个体转向估计总体使用频率，在可证明地保护用户隐私的同时，仍能实现对语言模型使用情况的准确估计。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Red-Green Sequence (RGS) locally differentially private watermark, which reconciles privacy with provenance by shifting the watermarking goal from tracking individuals to estimating aggregate usage, provably limiting individual privacy leakage while enabling accurate frequency estimation.
